"贝洛蒂所追求的，是在吉尔·桑德根基中那种千锤百炼的克制之美与“强烈的简洁”之中，植入一丝微妙的违和感。“多余”转变为不可或缺，“做加法”的行为与“做减法”的行为遥相呼应。通过让相互矛盾的元素共存，构建出一个碎片化且充满张力的视觉故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "故事并未预设明确的剧情。它弥漫着令人联想起希区柯克或赖纳·维尔纳·法斯宾德的气息，有意留下了抽象性，以便观者能够自由地填补其中的空白。坎贝尔和上田是在跑道上生活吗？他们是正准备启程，还是刚刚抵达？这种暧昧不清的境况本身，便构成了这组广告大片的悬念。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "视觉画面由霍沃斯操刀的短片中截取的静帧构成。粗粝的质感和令人联想起褪色VHS录像带的色调，捕捉到了紧张、兴奋以及直面内心的瞬间。此外，由Space Afrika feat. Deuén创作的《If This Is Hell》进一步放大了影像的碎片感与不安的氛围。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们希望用最少的手法，来表现出张力与惊奇，”贝洛蒂如是说。在保持吉尔·桑德一贯“以少胜多”美学的同时，这一次更向前迈出了一步，构建出一个带有阴影与官能性的世界。优雅与不安、克制与官能。在这些无法被完全解读的矛盾感之间，贝洛蒂率领的全新吉尔·桑德形象浮现而出。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
ジル サンダーが2026年秋冬キャンペーンを発表した。シモーネ・ベロッティによるクリエイティブ・ディレクションのもと、フォトグラファー／ディレクターのモニ・ホーワースが撮影。モデルにはエディ・キャンベルとウエダ ダイスケを起用している。

舞台となるのは、自家用飛行場の滑走路。そこにはラテックスで覆われたテーブルやアルミ箔に包まれたソファなど、本来は室内にあるはずの家具が野外に配置されている。明確な間取りも壁もなく、「住まい」という概念だけが断片的に残された空間。離陸と着陸の両方を受け入れる滑走路を、何かが始まる場所として描き出した。

ベロッティが追求したのは、ジル サンダーの根幹にある研ぎ澄まされた抑制美と「力強いシンプルさ」に、わずかな違和感を差し込むことだ。「余剰」が不可欠なものへと変わり、「加える」行為が「取り除く」行為と呼応する。相反する要素を共存させることで、断片的かつ緊張感に満ちた視覚的な物語を構築している。

物語には明確な筋書きが用意されていない。ヒッチコックやライナー・ヴェルナー・ファスビンダーを思わせる気配を漂わせながら、見る者がその空白を自由に補完できるよう意図的に抽象性を残した。キャンベルとウエダは、滑走路で暮らしているのか。これから旅立つのか、それとも到着したばかりなのか。その判然としない状況そのものが、キャンペーンのサスペンスを生み出している。

ビジュアルは、ホーワースが手がけたショートムービーから切り出されたスチールで構成。ざらついたテクスチャーと色褪せたVHSを思わせる色調によって、緊張や高揚、自己の内面と向き合う瞬間を捉えている。さらにSpace Afrika feat. Deuénによる「If This Is Hell」が、映像の断片性と不穏な空気を増幅させる。

「最小限の手法で、緊張感と驚きを表現したかった」とベロッティ。ジル サンダーらしい「少ない要素でより多くを表現する」という美学を保ちながら、今回はそこから一歩踏み込み、影と官能性を帯びた世界を構築した。エレガンスと不穏さ、抑制と官能。完全には解読できない相反する感覚のあいだに、ベロッティ率いる新たなジル サンダーのイメージが浮かび上がる。

article_text:
Quentin Tarantino gets brutally honest in Jay Glennie’s new book, “The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s Inglourious Basterds,” about his decision to fire Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert before production started on his 2009 revisionist World War II movie. Laurent ended up being rehired for the leading role of Shosanna Dreyfus, a French cinema owner seeking revenge against the Nazi officer who killed her family.

“Mélanie Laurent’s table read was terrible. It wasn’t good enough to be terrible,” Tarantino told the author (via People ). “The most exciting day of preproduction is for me the table read. That is the closest I get to seeing the movie for the first time. Up until then, it’s just been me reading all the scenes to myself or to a friend … so a table read with the whole cast is so exciting and so important to me. Well, Mélanie was terrible, so I fired her.”

Related Stories

Laurent called Tarantino days after the table read to get her job back. She told the director she was not feeling well at the time and that she planned to fly herself back to Germany and put herself up at a hotel in order to read for him again. Tarantino admired Laurent’s passion and agreed to “turn the clock back” and “return to square one” with her as long as she was willing to go through three days of rehearsal with him. Whatever Laurent did doing those fateful few days impressed Tarantino enough for him to give the role of Shosanna back to her.

“Let me just go on the record for everybody to know: I love Mélanie,” Tarantino said. “The fact of the matter is, if we were not talking about the making of ‘Inglourious Basterds,’ I would never think about the table read again for the simple reason Mélanie is my Shosanna. She did a wonderful job. But we have decided to dive deep into the making of the movie with this book, and this is an important part of its history. You know, we agreed, warts and all. So, if we had not agreed to talk about the shooting of the movie, it would be out of my mind, and I would never think about it again.”

Isabelle Huppert, however, was not so lucky. She was fired by Tarantino and her role of Madame Ada Mimieux, a woman who shelters Shosanna in Paris, was given to the iconic “In the Mood for Love” star Maggie Cheung. Huppert “didn’t show up” to the table read, Tarantino said. “So fuck it. I fired her. I mean, I love Isabelle Huppert — ‘Heaven’s Gate’ and all that — but there were issues with her contract. It just kept stalling. And then not coming to the table read. Well, we cast Maggie instead.”

“That invariably happens,” the director continued. “As far as I’m concerned, if you’re cast and you are not at that table, I don’t owe you jack shit! You can be fired, especially if I get excited by what somebody else did in your absence.”

Unfortunately, all of the scenes that included Madame Ada Mimieux were cut out of the movie because Tarantino felt they over-explained things too much to the audience. As the director said: “Maggie was fantastic in the movie, but you just didn’t need to know how Shosanna acquired the cinema. All we needed was a title card saying ‘Four Years Later’ and Shosanna explaining that she inherited it from her aunt.”

“Inglourious Basterds” world premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2009, where it won best actor honors for Christoph Waltz, and then opened in theaters that August, where it became a box office hit with $321 million worldwide. The film remains one of Laurent’s signature roles.

“I have no moral compass when it comes to giving roles to actors: They have to be right. They have to feel like they are right for the world I have created,” Tarantino said about his freewheeling approach to hiring and firing actors. “I have fired actors in the past. If it’s not right, it is not right. I don’t owe them shit. I owe my film the best actors I can find. Period.”

“The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s Inglourious Basterds” is now available for purchase.

article_text:
For composer Francesco Le Metre , the brief when first discussing Apple Original Films ‘ disability rights drama Being Heumann with director Siân Heder was to capture the spirit of its subject, activist Judy Heumann, through music.

With his score, he says, he was aiming for something “honest and intimate” — not “too big or too cinematic” — that reflected Heumann’s “personality, her drive, her humanity, but also at the same time, the impact that she had on the community.”

Related Stories

Siân Heder & The ‘Being Heumann’ Crew On Creating An Inclusive Film & Production Environment – Contenders London

2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Tonys, Guilds & More

One throughline to the score was the sense of a “call to action” — the “big punk rock,” DIY spirit of the ’70s, which Le Metre captured through drums. “We had to deconstruct the drumming a little bit, so we played very unconventional grooves, and then also the strings,” he explained in conversation at Deadline’s Sound & Screen Film. “We performed the strings with a guitar pick instead of col legno to convey the sense of punk rock and, again, the DIY spirit of the movement.”

Strings also helped, Le Metre said, to capture the sense of Heumann as someone with drive and racing thoughts who was moved to act fast. “I worked on a lot of string textures, kind of like these short phrases that were bouncing one to another. And I did the same thing with the melodic writing. When it came to her humanity as well, instead of writing a straight melodic line, I had small motifs interweaving into one another, to represent her thoughts or impulse.”

Being Heumann marks the Sicilian composer’s first collaboration with Heder, the director behind another inclusive disability-themed crowd-pleaser in Apple’s groundbreaking Oscar winner CODA . Ruth Madeley stars as Heumann, who in 1977, led disabled activists in an occupation of San Francisco federal offices, refusing to leave until the government implemented landmark disability-rights protections.

Others in the cast include Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, Rob Delaney, Ray Fisher, Michael Patrick Thornton and Daniel Durant. Heder directed and co-wrote with Rebekah Taussig, adapting Heumann’s memoir. Producers include Heder, Kevin J. Walsh, David Permut, John W. Beach and Kevin Cleary.

The film premiered at TIFF in September before being released in select theaters and on Apple TV this month.

It will be curated by Tom Eccles , executive director of the Center for Curatorial Studies and the Hessel Museum of Art at Bard College; Ruba Katrib , chief curator and director of curatorial affairs at MoMA PS1; Shabbir Hussain Mustafa, chief curator at the Singapore Art Museum; and Mark Rappolt, editor-in-chief of ArtReview . It will be staged primarily at ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture, with some works on view at Museum of Islamic Art (MIA) and in MIA Park.", "links": [{"text": "Tom Eccles", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/tom-eccles/"}, {"text": "Ruba Katrib", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/ruba-katrib/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Around 54 artists and collectives will feature in “Unruly Waters,” with 30 of them presenting new commissions. This specificity is true above all in the exhibition’s treatment of Qatar, with objects and artworks representing the nation’s place in past, present, and future global connections.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/7.jpg?w=400", "alt": "A still of a vista with a red sun at top, which is reflected in a sliver of water. article_text:
Rubaiaya Qatar, a new quadrennial that will open its inaugural edition at various venues across Doha beginning November 21, has announced more than 120 artists that will participate in the new initiative, presented by Qatar Museums in collaboration with ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture.

Unlike most other recurring art exhibitions, Rubaiaya Qatar will be made up of three separate shows at three different institutions and will also include a public art component.

“The inauguration of Rubaiya Qatar marks a defining moment in this change, with Doha as the stage on which contemporary art from our region and beyond is presented to the world,” Sheikha Alanood Al Thani, the quadrennial’s director, said in a statement. “Foregrounding non-Western perspectives, fostering ambitious new commissions and embedding deep ecological and historical research into its curatorial core, Rubaiya Qatar offers a fresh paradigm for international exhibitions of contemporary art.”

The lead exhibition will be “Unruly Waters,” which borrows its names from a book by historian Sunil Amrith. It will be curated by Tom Eccles , executive director of the Center for Curatorial Studies and the Hessel Museum of Art at Bard College; Ruba Katrib , chief curator and director of curatorial affairs at MoMA PS1; Shabbir Hussain Mustafa, chief curator at the Singapore Art Museum; and Mark Rappolt, editor-in-chief of ArtReview . It will be staged primarily at ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture, with some works on view at Museum of Islamic Art (MIA) and in MIA Park.

Around 54 artists and collectives will feature in “Unruly Waters,” with 30 of them presenting new commissions. They include Lawrence Abu Hamdan, Farah Al Qasimi, Meriem Bennani, Cao Fei, Nicholas Galanin, Shilpa Gupta, Saodat Ismailova, Ayoung Kim, Oscar Murillo, New Red Order, Selma Selman, and Wael Shawky.

“Establishing the framework for Rubaiya Qatar as a whole, the lead exhibition, Unruly Waters , is planetary in scope but highly specific in the geographies it explores,” the four curators said in a statement. “The artists it presents trace trade winds, monsoon rhythms, ocean currents, and digital communication networks—from ancient sea routes to the World Wide Web—to redefine ‘globalism’ through ecology and human movement, understanding it as a product of nature as much as of commerce. This specificity is true above all in the exhibition’s treatment of Qatar, with objects and artworks representing the nation’s place in past, present, and future global connections.”

Accompanying “Unruly Waters” is “Our Common Currents” at Katara QM Gallery. Curated by Rubaiya Qatar’s acting head of curatorial affairs Lina Patmali, the exhibition will respond to “Unruly Waters” and include work by 12 artists, four of which are commissions.

“In Our Common Currents , the artists featured explore how interconnected we are with the natural world,” Patmali said in a statement. “With a starting point being Qatar, the artworks presented have created connections with different geographical contexts.”

Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art will present “Seething Sea,” which will curated by Qatar Museums curator and Mathaf cofounder Wadha Al-Aqeedi, with assistant curator Loulwah Kutbi. Taking its name a line in the Qur’an, the exhibition will feature some 53 artists and collectives and over 80 works from Mathaf’s collections. The participating artists all have ties to the Middle East and include Hassan Sharif, Dia Azzawi, Sophia Al-Maria, Charles Hossein-Zenderoudi, and Monira Al Qadiri.

“For millennia, the people of the Gulf lived from the sea and understood it through faith and folklore,” Al-Aqeedi said in a statement. “This exhibition explores that relationship through the work of three generations of artists hailing from every shore of the Gulf, who have returned to the sea again and again: to experiment, to document, to celebrate, and now to mourn. What visitors will find is a reminder of all the sea has given, and a warning of impending doom.”

Finally, Rubaiaya Qatar will feature at least seven public art installations, including Rirkrit Tiravanija’s untitled 2025 (no bread no ashes) , which debuted at MIA Park last year, as well as a work by Ibrahim Mahama made for the forthcoming Art Mill Museum and a mural at the National Museum of Qatar metro station by Minerva Cuevas.

In a statement, Sheikha Reem Al Thani, the deputy CEO of ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture, Public Art, and Rubaiya Qatar, said, “Through ambitious commissions, exhibitions, public art and public programmes, Rubaiya Qatar creates opportunities for lasting collaboration and artistic innovation while reinforcing Qatar’s role as a place where ideas, perspectives and cultural practices converge. More than a platform for presenting art, Rubaiya Qatar is an investment in cultural production, international exchange and the relationships that will shape future generations of artists, thinkers and audiences.”

article_text:
A major work by a market titan will go under the hammer at Christie’s New York next month. Gustav Klimt ’s landscape Litzlbergkeller (1915–1916) is estimated at $60–80 million, which, if achieved, would put it among the Austrian artist’s top prices at public sale. The piece is guaranteed to sell, the house confirmed to ARTnews . It has been in the same private collection for nearly three decades; the seller is unnamed. It goes to auction at the house’s marquee November 17 evening sale of 20th- and 21st-century art.

The painting set a record for Klimt when the family of the current owner paid $14.7 million for it at Sotheby’s New York in May 1997 (at that time, it was listed under the title Litzlbergkeller am Attersee , by which it has also been known); adjusted for inflation, that’s about $30.9 million. At that sale, it came from the estate of Serge Sabarasky, a cofounder of New York’s Neue Galerie , just a few subway stops north of Christie’s Rockefeller Center saleroom, where the work will be offered after a quick jaunt (October 27–29) to the auctioneer’s Hong Kong showroom. (As it happens, the Neue Galerie, home to some major Klimt works, reopens November 12 after a construction project.)

“The inn of Litzlbergkeller sits at the water’s edge, between Klimt’s allover technique and abstraction, form and dissolution, prewar certainties and the unknown,” said Max Carter, global chairman of 20th and 21st-century art, in press materials.

Klimt’s auction record stands at $236.4 million, paid at Sotheby’s New York in November 2025 for his Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer (1914−16). Six of the Austrian’s top 10 prices at auction were fetched by landscapes; seven of his top 10 prices were notched in 2022 or after, helping to fuel a patchy art-market recovery weighted toward the top end, leading ARTnews to title its new Top 200 Collectors issue “ The Year of the Trophy .”

From 1900 until his death in 1918, Klimt often spent his summers in the Austrian countryside on the shores of Lake Attersee, pictured in the canvas on offer. “It was during his summers in Litzlberg, on the shores of Lake Attersee, that the artist developed his profound connection with the natural world,” wrote Sarah Belmont for ARTnews in reviewing his top prices, some of which were for landscapes painted there.

The canvas on offer presents a view focused on the Litzlberg Cellar, a brewery and inn on the north shore where Klimt stayed during his first several summers in the area, but actually dates from a decade after his move to a cottage on the lake’s southern shore. The artist partly based the composition on his own study via a telescope from the opposite shore and partly on postcard views, Christie’s points out.

“This landscape reads like a lyrical composition in three stanze—the forest with majestic, whispering oak trees; the house embraced by their foliage; the shimmering reflection in the lake,” said Giovanna Bertazzoni, chairman of Christie’s Europe, in a press release, calling the work “inestimable.”

The piece was commissioned by banker and entrepreneur Otto Primavesi, who, with his wife Eugenia, was a major patron of the arts and commissioned Klimt to paint two family portraits in 1912. It went by 1927 to Austrian photographer and anthropologist Hugo Bernatzik; then to Vienna collector Kurt Wieser, who owned it from the ‘30s until at least 1958; and from there to Sabarsky, a major promoter of Klimt’s work.

In its long life, it has hung on the walls of museums and institutions such as Secession Vienna; the Künstlerhaus in Vienna; the Musées Royaux des Beaux-Arts in Brussels; Palazzo Strozzi in Venice; Kunsthaus Zürich; and the Leopold Museum in Vienna.

Christie’s announcement of the Klimt consignment comes just days after the same house announced another work with an $80 million high estimate: a Wassily Kandinsky abstraction that is guaranteed to exceed the Russian-born artist’s current high. Also in October, the house announced a $100 million group of works from a “distinguished collector” that is reported to be the famed artist Jeff Koons.

The auctioneer’s main competitor, Sotheby’s, has not been without major consignments for next month. It will offer $450 million in works from the Blaquier family, led by a major Vincent van Gogh; a $100 million collection of works from the estate of Ted and Ruth Baum, led by paintings by Mark Rothko and Ed Ruscha; and a dozen works from bankrupt Miami hedge funder George Allen Weiss.

article_text:
Films and events

Create

Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff

This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Nanette Burstein

USA 2026. 90min

Courtesy of National Geographic

Language English

Access information

Friday 16 October 21:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Carl Sagan dedicated his life to understanding the universe and our place within it, inspiring millions of people to become more interested in worlds beyond our own. Drawing on archives and interviewing those closest to him, this touching tribute interweaves Sagan’s pioneering research – and boundless passion for activism and advocacy – with his complex private life and the personal and working relationship that would define his later life.

Chloé Trayner

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Perfect Road

By turns exhilarating and intimate, this documentary portrait charts nomadic cyclist Max Schnell’s attempt to complete an extreme journey through some of Europe’s highest mountain passes.

Concrete Turned to Sand

Shaped by the tidal rhythms of British Columbia’s oyster farms, this richly cinematic documentary, shot on 35mm, exists where labour, scientific inquiry and the living world meet.

Chronovisor

The film collective Cosmic Salon (Jack Auen and Kevin Walker) make their beguiling and assured feature debut, guiding us through hidden histories and uncanny landscapes of belief, mystery and the unknown.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "选角导演约翰·帕普西德拉对挑选克里斯托弗·诺兰电影的演员并不陌生。自2000年的《记忆碎片》以来，诺兰一直依赖帕普西德拉来为其项目选角，并通过彼此默契的速记方式找到拼图的合适碎片。对于诺兰改编自荷马史诗的《 奥德赛 》，帕普西德拉不得不组建庞大的演员阵容，将荷马的史诗搬上银幕。直到帕普西德拉读了剧本，他才意识到这是诺兰对荷马作品的改编。", "links": [{"text": "The Odyssey", "url": "https://variety.com/t/the-odyssey/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "“我不会收到任何提前通知，”帕普西德拉在分享他们合作过程的见解时说道。“他喜欢给我出一道随堂测验：‘你觉得谁合适？你觉得怎么样？’过程就是这样开始的。”帕普西德拉在萨凡纳艺术设计学院（SCAD）萨凡纳电影节的一场电影工艺座谈会上透露：“他的确谈到过自己希望奥德修斯是一个美国人。我们讨论了这样一个想法：他是一个普通工人中的工人，一个平民英雄。”", "links": [{"text": "SCAD Savannah Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/t/scad-savannah-film-festival/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕普西德拉接着说：“我们排查了我们通常会提及的那些常见演员。我们开始把目光凝聚在马特[·达蒙]身上，觉得这是一个非常棒的主意——对马特来说有所不同——而且他在《奥本海默》中的表现在那部电影里确实非常特别。”随着达蒙确定出演奥德修斯，其余的演员阵容也开始成型。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这块拼图的关键之一，是找到合适的女演员来饰演喀耳斯。在荷马的诗作中，喀耳斯是一位美丽的诱惑者，为了消遣而玩弄士兵。在诺兰的版本中，奥德修斯和他的手下遇到了喀耳斯，这是一个能将奥德修斯的手下变成猪的女巫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕普西德拉解释道：“她以一种面貌出现，然后又变成另一种样子；这就是她具备的女巫特质。我们讨论过好几位女演员，但萨曼莎[·莫顿]太棒了。她是一位勇敢的表演者。我想，当我们提出这个想法时，所有这些因素都完美融合了。克里斯对此一拍即合，因为他一直是萨曼莎的粉丝。你能真切地感觉到，她将为那个章节创造出非凡的东西——一些有趣、可怕，但在开头又展现出人类脆弱性的东西。”", "translated": "paragraph", "text": "米罗尼克解释说，她把一张草图发给了莫顿。“她非常开通，我们在草图中决定，她的女巫特质将会显现出来。她将是一个女性角色，但她的服装将同时暗示出男性和女性的特征。其中有皮革、皮带，最重要的是，她拥有从许多曾踏入她家门的人那里收集来的各种配饰。这让她深深扎根于过去。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", article_text:
Casting director John Papsidera is no stranger to casting Christopher Nolan films. Ever since 2000’s “Memento,” Nolan has relied on Papsidera to cast his projects and find the right pieces of the puzzle through their trusted shorthand. For Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic poem “ The Odyssey ,” Papsidera had to assembling a huge cast to bring Homer’s epic poem to life. It wasn’t until Papsidera read the script that he realized it was Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s work.

“I don’t get any heads-up,” Papsidera says, sharing insight into their collaborative process. “He loved to give me a pop quiz: ‘Who do you think? What do you think?’ And that’s how the process began.” Speaking at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival during a crafts panel on the film, Papsidera revealed, “He did talk about how he wanted Odysseus to be an American. We talked about the idea that he’s a worker among workers, an everyman.”

Papsidera continued, “We went through the usual suspects of actors we typically bring up. We started to coalesce around Matt [Damon], thinking it was a really great idea — different for Matt — and what he had done in ‘Oppenheimer’ was really special in that film.” With Damon in place as Odysseus, the rest of the cast began to take shape.

One crucial piece of the puzzle was finding the right actress to play Circe. In Homer’s poem, Circe is a beautiful temptress who toys with the soldiers for pleasure. In Nolan’s version, Odysseus and his men come across Circe, a witch who transforms Odysseus’ men into pigs.

Papsidera explained, “She appears one way and then turns into something else; that’s the witchlike quality of her. We talked about actresses, but Samantha [Morton] is brilliant. She’s a brave performer. I think all those things melded when we brought up the idea. Chris sparked to it because he’s always been a fan of Samantha. You just felt the sense that she was going to invent something remarkable for that chapter — something interesting, scary and still showing human vulnerability in the beginning.”

Joining Papsidera was the film’s production designer Ruth De Jong.

De Jong and Nolan scouted locations around the world. A fifth-century castle in Italy, perched approximately 1,030 feet above sea level, became Ithaca. She also designed multiple Trojan horses, each standing approximately 35 feet tall. The beaches of Essaouira, on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, served as the discovery site of the Trojan horse and the boat launch for Odysseus’s journey back to Ithaca. Troy, by the numbers, was a massive accomplishment — it covered more than 2.5 acres, or over 110,000 square feet, large enough to accommodate 2,000 extras and more than 60 structures.

For Circe’s part of the journey, De Jong said, “We absolutely did not want a Hansel-and-Gretel version in the woods. But we didn’t know where in the world Circe needed to land to work.” She explained that it wasn’t necessarily about using locations because they were Scotland or Morocco. “We were after the flora and fauna, the landscape and what the backdrop gave us. This just so happened to be Scotland.” De Jong continued, “Circe needed to be near the ocean. Odysseus and his men were hungry; they see smoke and go hunting. We settled on this cliff in the Scottish Highlands and constructed it right on the edge of the cliff. A few steps forward, and you’re straight down.” She added, “Chris and I grabbed onto the topography and I designed it all based on the craggy rocks that existed. We played with the idea that maybe she commandeered or took over this house we built — maybe someone else had been there previously. Maybe it was just a bunch of ruins that she had repurposed. We sculpted Athena’s head, added animals and just had a lot of fun with it.”

When it came to Circe’s costume, Ellen Mirojnick, the film’s costume designer, had a clear directive: like Calypso and Athena, Circe was a goddess. “Chris insisted that these goddesses were to be real — women who were independent and took care of themselves at all costs. There was nothing fantastical about it.”

Mirojnick explained that she sent a sketch to Morton. “She was so open, and in the sketch, we decided that her witchlike quality would be apparent. She’d be a female character, but her costume would indicate both male and female traits. There was leather, belts, and most importantly, she had different accouterments that she had collected from many people who had passed through her door. It rooted her in the past.”

Papsidera also discussed building out the family dynamic, including casting Tom Holland as Telemachus, Odysseus’ son and Anne Hathaway as Queen Penelope. “Anne was me,” he said. “Tom, we arrived upon. All of these people were the superheroes of their time. All of these characters needed to be larger than life. What we did in ‘Oppenheimer’ — giving faces to those scientists and not just letting them be anonymous — we did out of respect for the people in that atomic movement. Similarly, in ‘The Odyssey,’ these characters live in mythology, literature and people’s minds. To pay respect to that, we knew we had to cast them in a bigger way.”

He added, “When you boil down how many actors are really right for a role like Telemachus, you come to Tom pretty quickly. These characters, especially those Odysseus encounters on his journey, each have their own place and you want to meet them along the way and see who they are. It wasn’t about randomly casting names; it was about rooting the characters in reality while giving them the larger-than-life space they deserve as gods and goddesses.”

De Jong concluded the conversation by talking about the collaborative process with Nolan and described it as “playing basketball with Kobe Bryant.” She went on to say, “I love somebody who is going to the mat and not say, ‘That’s difficult.’ Every day was difficult on this job. Any one of us could go up to Chris and it’s open communication. Conversation is there, and it’s open.”

article_text:
A Brazilian outpost of Paris’s hallowed Centre Pompidou initially planned to open next year has been pushed back 2029, according to a report in the Art Newspaper .

Construction on Centre Pompidou Paraná, in the southern Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu, has not begun, and a planned call for bids has reportedly been pushed back from its expected date next month. A Pompidou spokesperson told TAN , “The project is currently working toward an opening in 2029 and is in the technical preparatory stages for the bidding process.”

A likely part of the reason for the delay is governmental change in the state of Paraná. The original deal was signed last year by governor Carlos Massa Ratinho Junior, with an investment of close to $50 million. But after an election earlier this month, his administration has changed to that of Sergio Moro. According to TAN , “During his campaign, the former federal judge—best known for the Lava Jato investigation that led to the current Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s imprisonment before his conviction was later annulled—pledged to continue the museum project.”

The Pompidou spokesperson said the change in the timeline “is to ensure that Centre Pompidou Paraná is established as a state cultural policy, rather than merely an initiative tied to a specific administration.”

The site planned for Centre Pompidou Paraná is near Iguazu Falls, a well-traveled UNESCO World Heritage site since 1984. The proposed building was designed by the Paraguayan architect Solano Benitez, and estimates for visitation to the museum are expected to amount to some 800,000 annually.
excerpt_original: Construction on the planned Centre Pompidou Paraná has not yet begun.

"雄性与雌性，竟然有如此大的差异！从极具视觉冲击力的标本与模型中探寻“性”之奥秘", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "步入展厅，首先映入眼帘的是各种逼真的动物剥制标本和模型。在将雄性和雌性并排陈列的展区，体格与外观的差异一目了然。长着气派鹿角的雄鹿，以及没有角的雌鹿。象征雄性狮子的鬃毛，在雌性身上也踪迹全无。另一方面，在自然界中，雌性体格大于雄性的物种也并不罕见。这种雄性和雌性外观上的差异被称为“性二型”，与围绕繁殖的竞争以及向伴侣展示自我等息息相关。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展现“性二型”的各种动物展示现场", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "让人惊叹的远不止动物。植物同样也拥有性别。其中最令人印象深刻的，是复原了香蕉雄花与雌花的逼真模型。朱红色的巨大花序（雄花）垂挂而下的姿态，既带有美感，又隐隐透出一股妖异的震撼力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/3-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "逼真的香蕉树模型。其洋溢着南国野性的姿态令人眼前一亮", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "香蕉是先开雌花，随后再开雄花。我们所食用的果实正是由雌花部分发育而成的。平时漫不经心送入口中的水果，竟然有着这样的机制，实在令人惊叹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，植物的性机制拥有与动物不同的复杂性。一朵花中同时具备雄蕊与雌蕊的、同一株植物上分别开出雄花与雌花的、以及分为雄株与雌株的，可以说是种类繁多。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/4-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "阐述植物“性”机制的图文展板。植物的性机制丰富多彩，丝毫不逊色于动物", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "唱歌、跳舞、战斗！生物惊人的求爱大作战", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在展览中，最能吸引众多目光的莫过于介绍求爱行为的专区。首先吸引人的是拥有华丽饰羽的大极乐鸟剥制标本。在繁殖期，大极乐鸟的多个雄性会聚集在被称为“求爱场（Lek）”的集体求婚场所，向雌性齐声展示自己。雄性会展开双翅在树枝间跳跃，当雌性靠近时，则会呈扇形展开黄色和白色的美丽饰羽进行舞蹈表演。这景象简直就像是一场集体的相亲大会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/5-13.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "在“求爱场”求爱的大极乐鸟剥制标本展示。", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "更让人惊叹的是园丁鸟的求爱行为。这种鸟类的雄性会用小树枝等搭建出被称为“凉亭”的结构物。不仅如此，它们还会用石头、贝壳以及色彩鲜艳的果实等将周围装点一番，在前来参观的雌性面前表演舞蹈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/6-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“凉亭”与园丁鸟雄性", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "凉亭并非用于育雏的巢穴，而是专门为求爱而建造的。建筑、装饰再加上舞蹈，生物的世界中竟然存在如此煞费苦心的求爱作战，着实令人惊叹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会求爱的可不只是鸟类。例如，栖息在澳大利亚的孔雀蛛会高高抬起色彩鲜艳的腹部，一边摇晃着腿一边跳起舞蹈。由当代艺术家玛丽亚·费尔南达·卡多佐（Maria Fernanda Cardoso）创作、在展会特设舞台上放映的影像作品《论艺术的起源 Ⅰ–Ⅱ》绝对不容错过。作品中精准捕捉了孔雀蛛独特的姿态及其独具一格的动作，并且在脚下的舞台上，连画面中四处移动的蜘蛛所引发的振动都被完美复现，让参观者能够通过五感切实体会到这种求爱舞蹈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/7-11.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "玛丽亚·费尔南达·卡多佐《论艺术的起源 Ⅰ–Ⅱ》摄影：青山谦太郎", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一方面，在围绕繁殖的竞争中，除了华丽的求爱，雄性之间也会展开激烈的争斗。展会现场通过逼真的剥制标本重现了熊和鹿的斗争。那仿佛随时会动起来的压迫感，让人真切感受到它们巨大的体型和锋利的角正是与延续生命的竞争紧密相连的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/8-11.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展会现场不仅有剥制标本，还播放着实际战斗的影像", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "唱歌、跳舞、打扮自己，有时甚至还会战斗。形式虽各有不同，但其背后都是生物们试图将生命延续至下一代的生命活动，这是一场能让人深切感受到这一点的展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "雄性变雌性，雌性变雄性！？颠覆常识的性机制", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "话虽如此，我们往往会认为雄性与雌性的区别自出生起便已注定，且终生不变。然而在生物的世界里，情况却并非总是如此。向我们揭示这一意外事实的，是一张拍摄于超市鲜鱼专柜的照片。单单在这张照片中，竟然就有足足5种鱼类，正经历着从雄性到雌性、或是从雌性到雄性的性转变。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/9-9.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "拍摄于国立科学博物馆筑波研究设施所在的筑波市某超市内的一张照片。在海鲜世界里，性转变并非罕见现象", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，红鳍东方鲀（注：此处指コブダイ/许氏猪齿鱼/石鲷等，原文コブダイ）是一种由雌性转变为雄性的鱼类。展览中可以看到随着性转变而导致头部逐渐隆起的过程模型。据解说介绍，红鳍东方鲀被称为“雌性先熟”，从幼鱼到年轻成鱼阶段首先作为雌性度过，其中特别巨大的“被选中”个体则会完成性转变成为雄性，随后长出肉瘤并形成后宫，与雌性进行生殖。这让人切实感受到生物的“性”比我们想象的要灵活得多。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/10-4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "更有趣的是一种名为绿豹蛱蝶（原文：メスグロヒョウモン）的蝴蝶标本，其身体正中央清晰分化并呈现出雄性与雌性的特征。左右翅膀的颜色和花纹截然不同，看起来就像是将两种不同的蝴蝶各取一半拼凑在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/11-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "绿豹蛱蝶的“雌雄莫赛克（Gynandromorph）”。左半边呈现雌性特征，右半边呈现雄性特征", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据说这是一种被称为“雌雄嵌合体（Gynandromorph）”的现象，由于构成身体的细胞性别在身体左右两侧各不相同而产生。到了这种地步，已经无法用单纯的雄性或雌性这一区分来解释了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当然，要理解这些性机制，还需要一些诸如染色体、基因以及细胞功能等略显艰深的科学知识。不过，对此大可放心的原因在于各处设置了运用漫画形式的解说展板。那些肉眼无法看到的复杂机制，通过通俗易懂的图画与说明变得易于理解，这实在令人感到欣慰。如果您觉得“解说有点难”，请务必先读一读漫画！", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/12-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展会各处准备了以漫画形式呈现的解说展板。通俗易懂，千万不要错过", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不仅如此，展览还集中展示了许多超乎我们想象的案例：既具备雄性和雌性双重功能的雌雄同体生物，无需受精就能繁衍的无性生殖案例，以及拥有2种以上“性”的真菌类等等。这些案例丰富得让人觉得“多样性”这个词已经完全无法概括，让人深刻体会到生物“性”的世界是如此广阔而深邃。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/13-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "第二展厅中介绍了颠覆我们“性”概念的藻类与菌类案例", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "路边盛开的花朵，超市鲜鱼专柜陈列的鱼类，公园里偶遇的鸟类。在这些我们漫不经心观赏的生物身上，各自隐藏着为了延续生命而令人惊叹的“性”世界。这是一场能让人充分体会到，在我们的日常生活之中居然潜藏着如此深奥生命活动的展览。非常推荐大家前去参观。（撰稿人：斋藤久嗣）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "特别展“生物的性”", "スーパーの鮮魚売り場に並ぶ魚介類のなかには、一生の途中でオスからメスへ、あるいはメスからオスへと性を変えるものが少なくありません。夜の田んぼから聞こえるカエルの鳴き声は、繁殖相手を呼び寄せるためのアピールでもあります。身近な生きものたちの姿や行動には、私たちが知らない驚くべき「性」の仕組みが隠されているのです。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "現在、国立科学博物館27年2月21日まで開催中の特別展「生きものたちの性」では、「性」という切り口で、生命の不思議や多様性に触れることができます。展示室には、動物や植物などの標本、模型、映像、音声を通して、生きものたちが命をつないできた驚くべき仕組みが詰まっていました。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "オスとメス、こんなに違う！ 迫力の標本や模型から探る性の不思議"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会場に入ると、まず目を引くのが、動物たちのリアルな剥製や標本の数々です。オスとメスを並べた展示では、体格や外観の違いが一目瞭然。立派な角を持つオスのシカと、それを持たないメス。ライオンのオスを象徴するたてがみも、メスには見られません。一方、自然界にはオスよりもメスのほうが体格の大きい種も珍しくないようです。こうしたオスとメスの外見の違いは「性的二型」と呼ばれ、繁殖をめぐる競争や相手へのアピールなどと深く関わっています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "「性的二型」を伝える様々な動物たちの展示風景", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "驚くのは動物ばかりではありません。植物にもちゃんと性があります。なかでも印象的だったのが、バナナの雄花と雌花を再現したリアルな模型でした。朱色の大きな 花序 （雄花）が垂れ下がる姿には、美しさとともに、どこか妖しげな迫力も漂います。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/3-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "リアルなバナナの木の模型。南国の野性味あふれる姿にハッとさせられる", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "バナナは、はじめに雌花が咲き、続いて雄花が咲きます。私たちが食べる果実は雌花の部分にできるものです。ふだん、何げなく口にしている果物にも、こんな仕組みがあったとは驚きでした。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "また、植物の性の仕組みは、動物とはまた違った複雑さを持っています。一つの花に雄しべと雌しべを備えるもの、同じ株に雄花と雌花が咲くもの、雄株と雌株に分かれるものなど、実にさまざまなのです。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/4-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "植物の「性」の仕組みを説明するパネル展示。動物に負けず劣らず、植物の性の仕組みもバラエティに富んでいる", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "歌って、踊って、闘う！ 生きものたちの驚くべき求愛作戦"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展示の中でも、とりわけ多くの人の目を引きそうなのが、求愛行動を紹介するコーナーです。まず惹かれたのが、豪華な飾り羽を持つオオフウチョウの剥製でした。オオフウチョウは繁殖期になると、複数のオスが「レック」と呼ばれる集団求婚場に集まり、メスに向けて一斉にアピールします。オスは翼を広げて枝から枝へと跳び回り、メスが近づくと、黄色と白の美しい飾り羽を扇状に広げてダンスを披露します。まるで集団のお見合いのような光景だな、と思いました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/5-13.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "「レック」で求愛するオオフウチョウたちの剥製展示。", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "さらに驚かされたのが、オオニワシドリの求愛行動です。この鳥のオスは、小枝などを組み合わせて「東屋」と呼ばれる構造物をつくりあげます。そして、周囲を石や貝殻、色鮮やかな果実などで飾り立て、訪れたメスの前でダンスを披露するというのです。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/6-12.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "「東屋」とオオニワシドリのオス", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東屋は子育てのための巣ではなく、求愛のためだけに作られます。建築に装飾、さらにダンスまで、生きものの世界に、これほど手の込んだ求愛作戦があるとは驚きでした。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "求愛するのは、鳥だけではありません。例えば、オーストラリアに生息するピーコックスパイダーは、鮮やかな色彩の腹部を持ち上げ、脚を振りながらダンスを披露します。会場内に特設されたステージで上映される、現代美術家マリア・フェルナンダ・カルドーゾによる映像作品《芸術の起源についてⅠ–Ⅱ》は必見。ピーコックスパイダーのユニークな姿やその独特の動きが克明にとらえられ、さらに足元のステージでは、画面を動き回るクモの起こす振動まで再現され、五感でその求愛ダンスを体感できる仕掛けになっていました。"}, article_text:
スーパーの鮮魚売り場に並ぶ魚介類のなかには、一生の途中でオスからメスへ、あるいはメスからオスへと性を変えるものが少なくありません。夜の田んぼから聞こえるカエルの鳴き声は、繁殖相手を呼び寄せるためのアピールでもあります。身近な生きものたちの姿や行動には、私たちが知らない驚くべき「性」の仕組みが隠されているのです。

現在、国立科学博物館27年2月21日まで開催中の特別展「生きものたちの性」では、「性」という切り口で、生命の不思議や多様性に触れることができます。展示室には、動物や植物などの標本、模型、映像、音声を通して、生きものたちが命をつないできた驚くべき仕組みが詰まっていました。

オスとメス、こんなに違う！ 迫力の標本や模型から探る性の不思議

会場に入ると、まず目を引くのが、動物たちのリアルな剥製や標本の数々です。オスとメスを並べた展示では、体格や外観の違いが一目瞭然。立派な角を持つオスのシカと、それを持たないメス。ライオンのオスを象徴するたてがみも、メスには見られません。一方、自然界にはオスよりもメスのほうが体格の大きい種も珍しくないようです。こうしたオスとメスの外見の違いは「性的二型」と呼ばれ、繁殖をめぐる競争や相手へのアピールなどと深く関わっています。

驚くのは動物ばかりではありません。植物にもちゃんと性があります。なかでも印象的だったのが、バナナの雄花と雌花を再現したリアルな模型でした。朱色の大きな 花序 （雄花）が垂れ下がる姿には、美しさとともに、どこか妖しげな迫力も漂います。

バナナは、はじめに雌花が咲き、続いて雄花が咲きます。私たちが食べる果実は雌花の部分にできるものです。ふだん、何げなく口にしている果物にも、こんな仕組みがあったとは驚きでした。

また、植物の性の仕組みは、動物とはまた違った複雑さを持っています。一つの花に雄しべと雌しべを備えるもの、同じ株に雄花と雌花が咲くもの、雄株と雌株に分かれるものなど、実にさまざまなのです。

歌って、踊って、闘う！ 生きものたちの驚くべき求愛作戦

展示の中でも、とりわけ多くの人の目を引きそうなのが、求愛行動を紹介するコーナーです。まず惹かれたのが、豪華な飾り羽を持つオオフウチョウの剥製でした。オオフウチョウは繁殖期になると、複数のオスが「レック」と呼ばれる集団求婚場に集まり、メスに向けて一斉にアピールします。オスは翼を広げて枝から枝へと跳び回り、メスが近づくと、黄色と白の美しい飾り羽を扇状に広げてダンスを披露します。まるで集団のお見合いのような光景だな、と思いました。

さらに驚かされたのが、オオニワシドリの求愛行動です。この鳥のオスは、小枝などを組み合わせて「東屋」と呼ばれる構造物をつくりあげます。そして、周囲を石や貝殻、色鮮やかな果実などで飾り立て、訪れたメスの前でダンスを披露するというのです。

東屋は子育てのための巣ではなく、求愛のためだけに作られます。建築に装飾、さらにダンスまで、生きものの世界に、これほど手の込んだ求愛作戦があるとは驚きでした。

求愛するのは、鳥だけではありません。例えば、オーストラリアに生息するピーコックスパイダーは、鮮やかな色彩の腹部を持ち上げ、脚を振りながらダンスを披露します。会場内に特設されたステージで上映される、現代美術家マリア・フェルナンダ・カルドーゾによる映像作品《芸術の起源についてⅠ–Ⅱ》は必見。ピーコックスパイダーのユニークな姿やその独特の動きが克明にとらえられ、さらに足元のステージでは、画面を動き回るクモの起こす振動まで再現され、五感でその求愛ダンスを体感できる仕掛けになっていました。

一方、繁殖をめぐる競争では、華やかな求愛だけではなく、オス同士が激しく争うこともあります。会場では、クマやシカの闘争をリアルな剥製で再現。今にも動き出しそうな迫力があり、巨大な体や鋭い角が、命をつなぐための競争と結びついていることを実感させられました。

歌い、踊り、着飾り、ときには闘う。形は違っても、その背景には次の世代へ命をつなごうとする生きものたちの営みがあるのだな、と実感させられる展示です。

オスがメスに、メスがオスに!? 常識を覆す性の仕組み

ところで、私たちはオスとメスの違いを、生まれたときから決まっていて、一生変わらないものだと思いがちです。しかし、生きものの世界では必ずしもそうではないようです。その意外な事実を教えてくれるのが、スーパーの鮮魚売り場を撮影した一枚の写真です。この写真のなかだけでも、じつに５種類もの魚が、オスからメスヘ、あるいはメスからオスヘと性転換しているのです。

また、コブダイはメスからオスへと性転換する魚ですが、展示では、性転換にともなって、頭部が徐々に盛り上がっていく途中経過を示す模型が見られます。解説によると、コブダイは「雌性先熟」といい、幼魚から若い成魚まではまずメスとして過ごし、その中で特に大きな“選ばれし”個体がオスへと性転換を遂げ、そしてコブを発達させハレムを形成してメスとの生殖を行うとのこと。生きものの「性」が私たちの想像以上に柔軟なものであることを実感させてくれます。

さらに面白かったのが、体のちょうど真ん中でオスとメスの特徴が分かれて発現したメスグロヒョウモンというチョウの標本です。左右の翅の色や模様が大きく異なり、まるで別々のチョウを半分ずつつなぎ合わせたように見えます。

これは「ギナンドロモルフ（雌雄モザイク）」と呼ばれる現象で、体を構成する細胞の性が体の左右で異なるために生じるとのこと。こうなると、もうオスかメスかという単純な区別では説明できません。

さて、こうした性の仕組みを理解するには、染色体や遺伝子、細胞の働きなど、少々難しい科学の知識も必要になります。しかし、そこで頼りになるのが、随所に設けられたマンガを使った解説パネルです。目には見えない複雑な仕組みも、親しみやすい絵と説明を通して、理解しやすいよう工夫されていたのは嬉しい限りでした。「解説が難しいな」と思ったら、まずはマンガを読んでみてください！

さらに展示は、オスとメスの両方の働きを持つ雌雄同体の生きものや、受精せずに増える無性生殖の事例、２つ以上の「性」をもつキノコ類など、私たちの想像の斜め上を行くような事例が目白押し。もはや「多様性」という一言では収まりきらないほど、広大かつ深淵な生きものの「性」の世界を、これでもかと見せつけられる思いがしました。

道端に咲く花、スーパーの鮮魚売り場に並ぶ魚たち、公園で見かける鳥たち。何げなく眺めていた生きものたちには、それぞれ、命をつなぐための驚くべき「性」の世界が隠されていたのでした。私たちの何気ない日常のなかに、これほど奥深い生命の営みが潜んでいるのだ、ということをたっぷりと教えてくれる展覧会です。ぜひ足を運んでみてはいかがでしょうか。（ライター・齋藤久嗣）

article_text:
Two key creatives have fallen out of Molepeople , Paramount’s new horror thriller co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal: star LaKeith Stanfield and director Rob Savage , who hands over the reins to English filmmaker Ben Wheatley .

Reasons for Stanfield’s departure haven’t been disclosed; Savage’s are chalked up to scheduling conflicts. We’re told the situation is amicable across the board.

Savage is fresh off the release of Other Mommy , a Jessica Chastain-led horror film for Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Universal, based on a novel by Josh Malerman, which while underperforming with critics, topped the domestic box office the weekend of October 9 and has grossed nearly $100M worldwide at time of reporting.

Related Stories

Keanu Reeves Circling James Wan's 'The Gangster, The Cop, The Devil' At Paramount

Francis Lawrence To Direct Sci-Fi Film 'Red Rising' For Paramount

In Molepeople , a man descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City, where he discovers a twisted society lurking beneath the streets. Paramount is set to distribute the film worldwide on August 27, 2027; they announced the casting of Stanfield and Ben Mendelsohn, who remains on board, the same day Other Mommy opened. It’s unclear whether to expect a shift in schedule, as reports had the film entering production in the UK as soon as the end of November.

Watch on Deadline

Penned by Savage’s Other Mommy collaborator Nathan Elston, Molepeople was developed independently, with Savage first announced as director in October 2024. Raphael Margules and J. D. Lifshitz, who were set to produce via their BoulderLight Pictures banner, brought the project into Paramount after being tapped to lead the studio’s new genre-focused label, Paramount Primal.

Jason Blum is producing alongside Lifshitz, Margules and James Harris. Ryan Turek and Tracy Rosenblum will exec produce alongside Savage and Elston.

A respected genre filmmaker, Wheatley most recently directed the Bob Odenkirk-led action thriller Normal , which released through Magnolia Pictures after premiering in the Midnight section of TIFF. Perhaps best known for the films Free Fire , executive produced by Martin Scorsese, and an adaptation of J.G. Ballard’s High-Rise — both for StudioCanal — he made his debut with Down Terrace , followed by Kill List , which earned six British Independent Film Award nominations, including Best Director and Best Screenplay. His filmography also includes a take on Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca for Netflix and Meg 2: The Trench for Warner Bros., among other projects. He is represented by WME, Independent Talent Group and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole.

Savage broke out with Host , an ingenious screenlife flick emerging from the Covid pandemic period, which released with Shudder and Vertigo Releasing. Subsequently, he’s helmed the horror flicks Dashcam and The Boogeyman for Momentum and 20th/Hulu, respectively. He is repped by Independent Talent Group, WME, Exile Entertainment and Jackoway Austen Tyerman.

Stanfield is coming off turns in Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters and Neon’s stoner comedy The Wrong Girls . Upcoming, he has Warner Bros.’ Taylor Sheridan-penned F.A.S.T. and John Lee Hancock’s Monsanto film for Netflix, among other projects. He is repped by CAA, Stark Management and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis.

article_text:
News

Danh Võ and Yohji Yamamoto Receive 13th Isamu Noguchi Award

DANH VÕ (left) and

YOHJI YAMAMOTO (right). Photos by Nick Ash and TAKAY. Courtesy the Noguchi Museum, New York.

On October 6, the Noguchi Museum announced Vietnamese-born artist Danh Võ and Japanese fashion designer Yohji Yamamoto as the recipients of its 13th Isamu Noguchi Award. Presented at the museum’s annual benefit—which this year coincided with the 75th anniversary of Noguchi’s iconic Akari light sculptures—the award honors individuals working across various disciplines, who share Noguchi’s experimental artistic ethos.

Võ, whose family fled Vietnam during the Cambodian-Vietnamese war (1978–89) and settled in Denmark, is a conceptual artist based between Berlin and Mexico City. His practice spans drawing, sculpture, and installation, often incorporating documents, photographs, and found objects with emotional or historical weight to explore questions of appropriation, identity, and collective memory. His work has been exhibited internationally, including at the Venice Biennale (2013, 2015, and 2019); the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York (2018); and the Pinault Collection at Bourse de Commerce, Paris (2023). Over the past decade, Võ has held multiple exhibitions engaging with Noguchi’s oeuvre, beginning in 2018 with “Noguchi for Danh Võ: Counterpoint” at the M+ Pavilion in Hong Kong and “Take My Breath Away” at SMK in Copenhagen. His most recent project is “Danh Võ in Situ: Akari by Noguchi” (2024– ) at the M+ museum.

Yamamoto is an internationally acclaimed fashion designer based between Tokyo and Paris, known for his avant-garde monochromatic garments featuring asymmetrical cuts and free-flowing silhouettes, which blend Western tailoring with Japanese minimalism. Throughout his nearly five-decade career, he has received several major accolades, including Japan’s Medal of Honor with Purple Ribbon (2004) and France’s Commandeur de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres (2011). Upon accepting the Isamu Noguchi award during the benefit, Yamamoto paid tribute to the late artist: “Isamu Noguchi created a language that opened up a space between East and West, and therefore beyond. I have always felt that creation should also exist somewhere between things, and thus in a space outside of apparent contradictions: between form and the body, strength and fragility, presence and absence.”

Eva Brank is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.

article_text:
木々の葉も色づき、季節の移ろいを感じる11月。東京では、無料で楽しめる魅力的な展覧会が多数開催されている。今月はInSitu2 – Ibasho（居場所）、日本国憲法展、森万里子展など、無料で気軽に訪れることができる展覧会を9件セレクトした。

「今はいつのことか―小村雪岱と玉山拓郎」｜資生堂ギャラリー（銀座・丸の内）

本展は、現代美術家・ 玉山拓郎 が、大正から昭和初期にかけて活躍した美術家・ 小村雪岱 の作品や思想から着想を得て制作した、新作インスタレーションを中心に構成される。1919年の開廊以来、銀座にある資生堂ギャラリーで、約100年の時を隔てた2人の表現が出会う。ニュースは こちら 。

会場： 資生堂ギャラリー 会期：11月3日～2027年2月28日

藤岡亜弥「Forget Me Not」｜BUG（銀座・丸の内）

藤岡亜弥 は、1972年広島生まれ。ニューヨーク滞在を経て、写真集『川はゆく』で、木村伊兵衛写真賞ほか多数受賞している。本展は、藤岡が9年前、オーストラリア・メルボルン在住の女性から、ある日本人女性の存在をめぐる一通のDM（ダイレクトメッセージ）を受け取ったことに始まる。地元の広島とメルボルン、ふたつの都市の戦後から現在をテーマに制作した作品を展示する。

会場： BUG 会期：10月14日〜11月29日

津田道子「からだの天気」｜慶應義塾ミュージアム・コモンズ（麻生台・虎ノ門）

美術家・ 津田道子 は、身体や映像を通して、世界を認識する方法を独自に探究してきた。近年は、レクチャー・パフォーマンスのようなランニング・イベント「and run」を展開するなど、運動を軸に知覚と身体性へのアプローチを深めている。本展では、津田が近年取り組むダイビングでとらえた海底映像をもとにした新作《呼吸の地質学》などを展示する。なお、津田が手がけた銀座メゾンエルメスのウィンドウ展示も開催中。こちらもあわせてチェックしたい。レポートは こちら 。

会場： 慶應義塾ミュージアム・コモンズ 会期：10月28日〜12月24日

冒険は、向こう側を覗く視線から始まる。津田道子が銀座メゾンエルメスのウィンドウに仕掛けたもの

アーティスト・津田道子が手がけるウィンドウディスプレイ「Looking Beyond - その向こう側へ」が公開中

「日本国憲法展2026」｜無人島プロダクション（清澄白河・両国）、青山｜目黒（恵比寿・代官山・中目黒）

1947年に施行された日本国憲法は、およそ80年を経たいま、政治的議論の中心にある。本展は、2会場で開催される。 無人島プロダクション では「シェルター」をテーマに人々のレジリエンスに焦点を当て、 青山｜目黒 では「スウェットショップ」をテーマに、権力が身体を規律し、労働を搾取して暴力を生み出す構造を検証する。対照的な周辺地域の戦後史を手がかりに、憲法の理想と現実社会との隔たりを問う。

会場： 無人島プロダクション 、 青山｜目黒 会期：11月4日〜11月29日

森万里子「Unity」｜SCAI PIRAMIDE（六本木・乃木坂）

森万里子 は、90年代半ばより国際的なアートシーンで注目を集め、以来、多領域にわたる実践を展開してきた。本展は、30年に及ぶ森の活動を包括する展覧会 「森万里子：燦燦」 が 森美術館 で開催されるのに合わせ、同時開催される。森の重要な着想源である「光」をテーマにした同名の連作を中心に構成される。

会場： SCAI PIRAMIDE 会期：11月5日〜12月19日

鈴木ヒラク「海と内臓」｜Yutaka Kikutake Gallery（六本木・乃木坂）

鈴木ヒラク は、「ドローイング」を絵と言葉のあいだに位置づけ、平面、彫刻、映像、パフォーマンスなど様々な媒体を横断しながら、「線」の表現の可能性を探究してきた作家。本展では、深海や宇宙を想起させる青を背景とした《海と記号》と、赤い顔料を背景とした《Interexcavation》という、対照的な色彩の二連作の新作を展示する。

会場： Yutaka Kikutake Gallery 会期：10月24日〜12月12日

「InSitu2 – Ibasho（居場所） 」｜エスパス ルイ・ヴィトン東京（表参道・青山）

「InSitu2」は、現代のクリエーションを促進する共通のプログラムとして、東京、ミュンヘン、北京のエスパス ルイ・ヴィトンを結ぶプロジェクト。東京では「居場所」をテーマに、物理的な空間という意味だけでなく、そこでなされる行為やひととき、呼び起こされる記憶によって変容する「居場所」の在り方を探る。本プログラムでは、日本の伝統芸能や話芸から、コンテンポラリーな音楽セッションまで、多岐にわたるパフォーマンスを実施。トークイベントや子供向けワークショップも開催する。レポートは こちら 。

会場： エスパス ルイ・ヴィトン東京 会期：10月24日〜11月27日

多彩なプログラムで、コミュニティを育む。「InSitu2 – Ibasho（居場所）」（エスパス ルイ･ヴィトン東京）レポート

GROUPによる空間で落語や能、DJイベント、トークなど多彩なアクティビティを展開。会期は10月24日〜11月27日

渡辺明日香 「ANIMATE」｜TOKYO INTERNATIONAL GALLERY（天王洲・品川）

渡辺明日香 は、アートやデザイン、アートディレクションなど幅広い領域で制作し、動植物や風景を平面的でインパクトのあるかたちと鮮やかな色彩で表現している。本展のタイトル「animate」には、アニマ──魂や生命──そのものの感覚といった意味がある。本展では、渡辺の色とかたちによる構成が生み出す作品世界を紹介する。

会場： TOKYO INTERNATIONAL GALLERY 会期：11月7日〜12月26日

「国際美術展 TOKYO ATLAS」｜アイルしながわ、WHAT MUSEUMほか（天王洲・品川）

「ARTE TOKYO」の一環として、東京・臨海エリアを舞台に開催される国際美術展。台場、青海、天王洲など、水辺の都市空間に国内外のアーティストが集い、アートを通して東京の新たな風景を描き出す。タイトルの「TOKYO ATLAS」には、神話的存在としてのアトラスと「地図帳」の意味が重ねられている。作品を鑑賞するだけでなく、アートが示す地図をたどりながら、東京という都市をあらためて読み解く機会となる。レポートは こちら 。

会場：台場公園、お台場海浜公園、 青海南ふ頭公園、地下駐車場（青海南ふ頭公園内）、 テレコムセンタービル 、 アイルしながわ 、 WHAT MUSEUM 会期：10月10日〜12月20日 ※一部有料プログラムあり

東京・臨海部で初開催、国際美術展「TOKYO ATLAS」が開幕。都市の風景に介入し、歴史や記憶を呼び覚ます

草間彌生の巨大バルーンやイケムラレイコの水上彫刻も。一部プログラムを除き観覧無料、会期は12月20日まで

article_text:
“ Tangles ” won the Grand Jury Prize at the 9th annual Animation Is Film Festival . Directed by Leah Nelson, the 2-D animated film follows a family impacted by their mother’s battle with dementia.

“We loved the fluid 2D animation which uses a stark monochrome framing to bring to life the personal story of a family impacted by the mother’s battle with dementia,” the features jury said. “We were especially impressed with how director Leah Nelson and her perfectly cast voice team were able to remain faithful to Sarah Leavitt’s graphic novel which tackles a serious, painful subject with great beauty, honesty, and a gentle touch and also offers a great flashback to 1990s-era San Francisco.”

What to Watch on Netflix in November 2026

Why Did Netflix Boot Bela Bajaria?

The Fumi Kitahara Special Jury Prize was awarded to “Iron Boy,” directed by Louis Clichy. The award was named in memory of publicist and champion of AIF’s mission Fumi Kitahara, who died in 2025. The film also won the Features Audience Award.

The jury said: “’Iron Boy’ is pure beauty from the medium we all love. Louis Clichy’s ‘Iron Boy’ was an easy stand-out thanks to its beautifully crafted water-color-like and Chinese ink-brush style visuals and how it told a story inspired by the director’s own memories of growing up in rural France. We also admired the way Clichy conveyed a world of emotions with his impressionistic visuals as well as his depiction of a young boy’s personal struggles with a physical handicap and the heartfelt portrayal of a strained father-and-son relationship which avoids sentimentality and the pitfalls of a traditional coming-of-age story.”

“Paper Trail,” directed by Don Hertzfeldt, won the Shorts Jury Grand Prize. The jury described the film as “unique and profoundly moving.”

The Shorts Special Jury Prize went to “Please,” directed by Anna Mantzaris. The jury called it “a wonderfully made, funny, and tender film that captures the absurdity and very human longing for connection.”

The 2026 feature competition lineup included “Cherry and Virgin” (Masanao Kawajiri), “Ghost — End of Night” (Shingo Natsume), “Iron Boy” (Louis Clichy), “Jim Queen” (Nicolas Athané and Marco Nguyen), “Julián” (Louise Bagnall), “O Filho Da Puta (Son of a Bitch)” (Otto Guerra, Érica Maradona, Tânia Anaya and Sávio Leite), “Tangles” (Leah Nelson), “The Violinist” (Ervin Han and Raúl García) and “Viva Carmen!” (Sébastien Laudenbach).

The shorts in competition this year were “Acid City” (Jack Wedge and Will Freudenheim), “Because Today is a Saturday” (Alice Eça Guimarães), “Blessed” (Birute Sodeikaite), “Core Dump” (Alona Rodeh), “Daughters of the Late Colonel” (Elizabeth Hobbs), “God is Shy” (Jocelyn Charles), “Hag” (Anna Ginsburg), “It’s Not a Phase Mom” (Nataël Renault, Tianhui Song, Anna Watson, Léa Mau-Glicenstein, Riley Cords and Reni Park), “Living With a Visionary” (Stephen P. Neary), “Paper Trail” (Don Hertzfeldt), “Paradaïz” (Matea Radic), “Please” (Anna Mantzaris), “Saba” (Liron Topaz), “Tuna Tartare” (Lena Greene), “Ultra Strong” (Catherine Lepage), “What We Leave Behind” (Jean-Sébastien Hamel and Alexandra Myotte), “With Tapes and Toasts in the Car” (Kiana Naghshineh) and “Winter in March” (Natalia Mirzoyan).

Over its four days, this year’s Animation Is Film Festival also included the first big-screen presentation of Dana Terrace’s “Knights of Guinevere,” a special screening of Laika’s “Wildwood” with director Travis Knight, a behind-the-scenes look at Disney’s “Hexed” and a presentation of work-in-progress “Clara and the Below,”

article_text:
[Editor’s note: This review was originally published on May 16, 2026 during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Neon will release the film in theaters Friday, November 13.]

It’s the final weekend of summer in 1986, upwardly aspirant Jewish families across Queens are still crowding around country club pools to make sure they get their annual money’s worth, and — in a little less than two months — the Mets are going to win the World Series for what might be the last time in team history. But nebbishy engineer Irwin Pearl ( Miles Teller ) doesn’t know that yet. He doesn’t know that this is his golden age. He doesn’t know that this is as good as it’s ever going to get.

What Irwin knows is that greed is good. That the income gap is widening at an unprecedented rate, that economic mobility is slowing to a crawl, and that his giant older brother Gary ( Adam Driver ) — a divorced ex-police officer who swans around the city like a majestic bird in a blue Mercedes — has started to make him feel even smaller than usual. What Irwin knows is that his mother-in-law wants him to move the family to Great Neck, that the older of his two bickering teenage sons wants an expensive party for his 18th birthday, and that his beautiful wife Hester ( Scarlett Johansson ) wants fewer things to worry about. Irwin isn’t the overly ambitious sort, but a man can only live in the suburbs of Mt. Olympus for so long before it starts to feel like the gods are taunting him to claim a small piece of it for himself.

And so the stage is set for James Gray’s deft and devastating “ Paper Tiger ,” a Jewish-American tragedy in a teapot that — like all of the writer/director’s best films — is both sweepingly mythic and hauntingly personal all at once. That double effect, once a magic trick that Gray’s movies would manage to pull off by the time they ended, has since become the de facto starting condition of his singular auto-cinema, which continues to pick at his formative wounds by processing them through the classics.

As indebted to Aeschylus as “Ad Astra” was to Joseph Campbell, or “The Lost City of Z” was to Henri Rousseau, “Paper Tiger” begins with a telling quote from the ancient playwright’s most famous text: “Let there be wealth without tears; enough for the wise man who will ask no further.” Even more telling, however, is the opening shot that follows, which surveys the same reedy marshland — or at least one identical to it — from the end of “We Own the Night.” It’s no surprise that a project first conceived as a direct sequel to 2022’s “Armageddon Time” should point back to Gray’s previous work, but never before has it been so clear, so fast, that he’s trying to process his own, highly specific experience by assimilating it into the curriculum that first taught him how to make sense of the world. The more acutely self-referential his films get, the more broadly they speak to the soft and immortal agony that propels their characters forward.

It’s an agony that goes by many (sur)names, but is colloquially referred to as “family.” “Paper Tiger” is many things, chief among them a textbook parable about the American Dream, a breathless thriller about a working-class schmuck who gets mixed up with the Russian mafiya, and a pleasantly open question about why Miles Teller has rededicated his career to cosplaying as “Lost in America”-era Albert Brooks (to my mind, a canny, convincing way of aging up the nonconformist spunk that first defined his screen image in the days of “Whiplash” and “The Spectacular Now”). But, at its most nuclear level, “Paper Tiger” is — to an even more explicit degree than “Little Odessa,” “The Yards,” and any of the other James Gray movies that it hungrily mulches into something all its own — a remarkably knowing and perceptive film about how family is, and has always been, the ultimate devil’s bargain. Our greatest strength and our heaviest cross to bear. The reason our most dangerous risks can seem worth taking, and the most valuable thing we risk by taking them.

Irwin gives “Paper Tiger” its shape, but it’s how Gary navigates those dilemmas that gives the film its soul. Heartbreakingly portrayed by Adam Driver in a career-best performance that stretches across flash, menace, and pure sincerity like a foot stepping down on a bed of nails without drawing blood, Gary is a vintage ’80s showboat who only knows how to show affection by offering to share in his apparent success. He strides into Irwin and Hester’s living room — after months of radio silence — with the razzle dazzle of a local celebrity and a fully catered feast from Peter Luger’s Steak House in tow for good measure. Irwin’s sons marvel at the gun their uncle still keeps holstered around his ankle (cool!), and his wide-eyed wife looks across the kitchen table and imagines what her life might have been like had she held out for the shinier Pearl.

At least, that’s what Irwin seems to imagine that his wife is imagining, though he’d sooner let such fears fester inside of him for the rest of his natural life than to speak them aloud. For all of the character’s frustrated aspirations for a better life, Teller endows him with the wizened humility of a second-generation Jewish immigrant who knows that it would be gauche to forsake what his late father-in-law — tempting to picture as Anthony Hopkins for continuity’s sake — sacrificed to make possible for their family. Irwin might even be smart enough to recognize that his brother is an empty promise in a tailored suit, but, in a less literal expression of the double vision that will soon cause his wife to crash her car into a tree, being smart isn’t the same as seeing things clearly.

Whatever the case, Irwin is powerless to resist his brother’s sales pitch when Gary lures him into the basement to reveal the reason purpose of his visit: An ambitious new business venture is seeping its way into the Gowanus Canal, and it could use a sharp engineer to help facilitate their plans for the waterway. Still connected to the gills after getting rich in the private sector, Gary doesn’t tell his naive kid brother that said venture is the Russian mob, but the beauty of it is that he doesn’t have to. It can just be another one of the many different things that Irwin doesn’t know. He’ll go down there, sketch a few diagrams for some bald and scary men straight out of central casting, and take home a healthy paycheck to his family (“Paper Tiger” won’t score any points for bucking mafia stereotypes, as Gray plays up their ruthlessness in order to stress how far Irwin is out of his depth).

The only problem is that Irwin takes the job as seriously as he would any other, and — to his profound regret — takes his two sons to go scope out the canal one night, where they see the Russians illegally dumping their waste into the water. The Russians don’t like that. They don’t know what he’s doing there. And, in the aftermath of a stomach-churning stick-up that twisted my guts with the queasy horror of a repressed memory, Gary is given a week to make the problem go away. Spoiler alert: Appeasing the leader of an organized crime ring isn’t as simple as cutting a check, and wouldn’t be even if Gary had access to $125,000.

It doesn’t take long for things to spiral out of control from there, as Irwin and his boys soon find themselves in the crosshairs of a turf war they are comically ill-prepared to survive, while Hester — kept in the dark for her own protection — is thrust into a different crucible that she chooses to keep secret from her husband for similar reasons. (Despite being heavily affected by period drag, Johansson’s performance is too limpid to be mistaken for caricature, growing more hollowed out and heartsick with every scene until it assumes the same void-like power that Brad Pitt once found in the farthest reaches of outer space.) Plotted with a fatalistic velocity that would make Aeschylus proud, Gray’s script corkscrews towards ruin at a sickening pace, its slick road to hell paved with a well-textured mixture of imperfect intentions.

For all of the red meat that “Paper Tiger” gets to chew off the bone, this is still a small and maybe slightly underfunded movie, its outsized impact only made possible because of the micro-details that Gray traces within and between his characters. And I’m not talking about the assortment of beepers and TaB cans, or the load-bearing shots of ’80s New York, which are all Joaquín Baca-Asay’s 35mm cinematography needs to complete the illusion of time travel. While the film is buttressed by a handful of exquisite setpieces (including a nightmarish home invasion sequence that transposes the film’s title into a piece of shadowplay, and a climactic shoutout that binds it even closer to the rest of Gray’s body of work), it’s ultimately fueled by the atomic frictions inside Driver’s performance.

To that point, the real tragedy of “Paper Tiger” isn’t that messing with the mob tears these brothers apart, but rather that it brings them together. There’s not a lot of time for fun and games, but it’s never lost on Gray that this is the most time Gary and Irwin have spent with each other in years — maybe even since they were kids. “We’ve never played in the dirt,” Gary tells Irwin as he lies to his brother about how everything about the Gowanus deal is above board. But they’re playing together now. The worse things get, the more they expose the extraordinary bond that allowed things to get so fucked up in the first place (a dynamic that becomes all the more wrenching because of how Gray transposes it onto Irwin’s sons). The worse things get, the more this movie sympathizes with Gary and Irwin for their parts in it.

It’s not that Gary is trying to do something nice for his brother, or that he’s shamelessly using Irwin to broker a lucrative deal with the Russians, but rather that everything that happens after that fateful offer stems from an inextricable braid of love and leverage. Gray is no stranger to saga about fraternal strains, but never has he so forcefully tugged at the ties that bind, or more sensitively observed how they can suffocate an entire family when a certain force pulls on them hard enough.

“Paper Tiger” is a story about a household gripped by a self-inflicted event that chokes the life out of its lungs, and precious few films have better conveyed what it feels like when the oxygen gets sucked out of a home without any hope of coming back. “We already had everything,” Irwin will eventually mutter under his breath. The deepest cut of this unshakeable tragedy is that, for the very first time, it leaves him begging for more.

Grade: A

“Paper Tiger” premiered in Competition at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. NEON will release it in theaters later this year.
excerpt_original: Like all of James Gray's best films, "Paper Tiger" is both sweepingly mythic and hauntingly personal all at once.

title_original: Un teatro di fragilità e vitalità: intervista all’attrice Valentina Picello
editorial_title_zh: 脆弱与生命力的剧场：专访演员瓦伦蒂娜·皮切洛
editorial_excerpt_zh: 瓦伦蒂娜·皮切洛（Valentina Picello）向我们讲述了她对剧场的理解以及她的舞台表演方式，从她的最新剧作到与卡斯特卢奇（Castellucci）和龙科尼（Ronconi）的合作，其间提及路易丝·布尔乔亚（Louise Bourgeois）、卡罗尔·拉玛（Carol Rama）与弗兰西丝·伍德曼（Francesca Woodman）。文章《脆弱与生命力的剧场：专访…

Pleuteri）编剧、爱丽丝·西尼加利亚（Alice Sinigaglia）执导、并与维托·维奇诺（Vito Vicino）共同演绎的剧作，将于10月27日至11月1日重返米兰小剧场协会（Teatro dell’Elfo）的法斯宾德厅（Sala Fassbinder）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": Lidi）执导的田纳西·威廉斯（Tennessee Williams）作品《热铁皮屋顶上的猫》），她穿梭于不同的剧作和导演视野之中，同时保持着极具辨识度的存在感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《安娜·卡佩利》、《母亲》以及《热铁皮屋顶上的猫》中，她展现出一种呈现出不同形态的生命力，即便在角色看似走投无路时也是如此。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Valentina-Picello-11.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你认同这种解读吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«是的，无论是在个人层面还是在剧本以及指导我的导演身上：他们引导我以积极的态度穿梭于人类深渊的降临之中。就好像我在面对这些时并不感到孤单。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我也相信，死亡中存在着某种具有救赎性、和解性的东西。我的角色往往比我们在现实生活中更早地察觉到这一点：他们找到了应对孤独的答案。有人将这种生命力称为讽刺或自我讽刺，但我认为这是那些很早就遭遇死亡的人所学会的东西。这是一场能够达成和解的对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我在我父亲去世前看到了这一点，当时他在和那些已经不在人世的人说话。我不知道该怎么称其为好，也许是一种清醒梦。不一定是指天堂的概念，而是指那些挚爱的人，他们比我们更早地看到了我们尚未看到的东西。这让人感觉不再那么孤单。这种感受也拯救了我自己。»", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "脆弱、讽刺、表面上的纯真：这些都是评论界对你的工作予以肯定的特质。有没有哪个角色能够展现出其他人尚未在你身上发现的特质？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«在我看来，它快要来了。我认为那就是1月份在卡梅洛·里菲奇（Carmelo "text": "«这是一场魔术。迭戈被我视为某种意义上我未曾拥有也永远不会拥有的儿子。我是在一次工作坊期间认识他的，当时他还在读高中，但他已经对戏剧和艺术充满热情并且开始写作了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他是我唯一的学生。一起成长是一件令人愉快的事。最初我辅导他是因为他想考入学校成为一名演员。后来我对他说：“迭戈，我认为你应该尝试成为一名剧作家。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在新冠疫情期间，我们利用那些异地相处几个月的时间进行练习，他开始构思《母亲》。一开始是我对他说：“这个儿子仅仅是一个功能性角色，它让母亲得以展开她的独白。要么你把它写成独白，要么我们就把儿子的部分展开，让它变成一段对话。”我们在电话里进行了持续的探讨。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "后来我们在丁达罗·格拉纳塔（Tindaro Granata）主持的“戏剧局势”（Situazione Drammatica）活动中进行了朗读，我们发现人们对此很感兴趣。他们原本期待的是母亲和儿子之间的一场自然主义对话；然而这却是一部关于记忆、回忆、语言和词汇的剧作。»", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "当爱丽丝·西尼加利亚和维托·维奇诺加入这段对话时发生了什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«我想信任迭戈。在经历了这么长时间之后，我只能信任他。一开始，爱丽丝和维托对我都有些敬畏，因为他们不认识我。他们以为会来一位“首席女演员”（“la prima attrice”）。我想到了第三天，这一切就已经烟消云散了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们一直都在一起工作，迭戈也在场，负责声音和灯光的人也都在。这部剧是我们所有人共同搭建的。迭戈很感激我们，因为如果只留在纸面上，没有导演的疯狂或是我的即兴发挥，它或许会显得过于形而上。因此它依然保留了一定程度的形而上沉浸感，但同时也非常有生命力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这两年里，我们做了小幅度的修改。把它带到非剧场空间帮助了我们：我们删减了一些不必要的部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以前我们害怕在没有爱丽丝和迭戈的情况下进行重演；而现在我们非常独立。维托不再害怕和我一起做出疯狂的举动。同事之间需要相互了解，除了理解文本的潜力之外。一开始，也许出于单纯，你会不惜一切代价把所有东西都塞进去。后来你发现简单胜于一切，但要做到这一点，你必须付出数月的努力。»", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你最初是通过在私人住宅里进行“帽子戏法”式的表演开始戏剧生涯的，并且在从皮科洛剧院（Piccolo）毕业后依然坚持这样做。那种与观众的亲近感教会了你什么？在大型舞台上你还在寻找它吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«是的，我在寻找家，也在寻找家人。我喜欢走进人们的家中，被收养几天。通常他们会在演出前一天就接待我们；演出结束后我们会煮意大利面，有些观众会留下来。排演期间，祖母和孩子们会走进来：我们参与到了那些日常生活的互动中，这让我感觉不那么孤单。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我锻炼出了一种被近距离观看时的某种厚脸皮，无论好坏，因为我在没有灯光的情况下就在那里。时至今日，有些演出仍允许我让观众几乎置身于舞台之上：在《Anna Cappelli》中往往就是这样。但我也很喜欢那个每次都会更新的家庭。我的精神上需要它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Ph.-Capitani_2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当你为了罗密欧·卡斯特卢奇（Romeo "“这些相遇必须放在它们发生的人生阶段来看。幸运的是，卡斯特卢奇和龙贡，我和他们同时工作，他们对我说的是同一件事：那场演出是一次经历，它不一定非要成为我所拥有的戏剧风格。我不需要在心理层面上挖得那么深，因为罗密欧寻找的并不是那种契合度。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我被选中是因为我有一具神经性厌食症的身体：他需要那具身体。不过，在试镜之后，罗密欧给了我一份他关于阿尔托的残酷戏剧对他的意义的手稿。我在其中读到的不是多少理论：而是具象的例子，对视觉艺术的参考，他正是出身于视觉艺术。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这两位风格迥异的大师，在同一时期遇到，他们向我发出了同样的危险警告，并帮助我保护了自己。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "角色也是图像。当你阅读它们时，你是如何在脑海中创造它们的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“在做戏剧之前，我想成为一名画家或雕塑家。我几乎立刻就放弃了：我还记得面对粘土的下午那种极致的孤独。我对自己说：‘可我真是无聊透顶啊！’", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，这种冲动留了下来：当我面对一个角色时，为了不以全副武装的强硬姿态闯入心理层面并伤害自己，我是通过对图像、具象灵感的搜寻来发展它的。我会去看我需要看的展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我和卡斯特卢奇合作时还很年轻。去美国演出，抵达芝加哥当代艺术博物馆并遇到不同文化的人，这是一种开放，通向一种不局限于某个单一导演或国家的戏剧，不一定仅仅建立在言辞上、某种高级言辞之上的戏剧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在剧团里，每个人都信任罗密欧。人们在不了解他的情况下经常说，他利用了别人。根据我的经验，事实并非如此。那些人可以决定自己的人生要做什么。如果一个人想伤害自己，即使关在自己的房间里也可以做到；而旅行并结识其他人可能是一段更好的经历。罗密欧从来不想拯救任何人，但也绝不想利用任何人。我认识的是一个诚实的人。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哪些女性艺术家滋养了你的探索？在文本之外，她们让你发现了什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我可以告诉你最近几场演出的参考对象。她们通常是那些直到年迈时才被认可为艺术家的女性。在这其中肯定有路易丝·布尔乔亚（Louise Bourgeois），她是画家、作家，尤其是雕塑家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我对外在她那些《Cells》（单元）很感兴趣：由私人物品或简陋材料构建的微型环境。她的父母从事壁画工作，她讲述自己小时候剪碎布料来遮挡那些被认为是不雅的形象的生殖器。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在她的一本书中，她还讲述了当父亲剥着橘子对她说‘这是一个阴道，它是这样打开的’时，是什么样的想法穿过了她的脑海。在她的作品中，我重新找到了对一个还在困惑的小女孩脑海中事物的追溯性视角。她的雕塑有很多乳房、巨大的阴茎。我对这种不压抑性欲和身体展示的方式很感兴趣，同时也对作为布景地点的单元感兴趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "还有卡罗尔·拉玛（Carol Rama）。她所描绘的床上的女性非常美：你永远分不清她们是在分娩还是在遭受电击。在那里，同样有一种对女性痛苦的升华。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "还有弗朗西斯卡·伍德曼（Francesca Woodman）。我非常喜欢她运动中的照片。例如，我喜欢我的演出由卢卡·德尔·皮亚（Luca Del Pia）拍摄。他并不总是那种‘场刊风格’的摄影师，因为一切都在动。他主要拍摄舞蹈，并且与卡斯特卢奇合作了一生。有些人不喜欢他，因为他们需要干净的照片来登在报纸上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他还拍摄了里菲奇（Rifici）的《俄瑞斯忒亚》（Orestea）：我还没看过那些照片，而且我充满了好奇。像往常一样，他走上舞台，进入布景。从美学上讲，那场演出简直是个炸弹。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你对这些身体的表征感兴趣的是什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“男人们认为那些他们无法了解的事情是理所当然的：初潮时的感受、分娩，直到月经不再来临的那一刻。我们看到的所有那些血，我们把手伸进去的血，他们并不了解，并且往往让他们感到恶心。我喜欢不压抑这种经历的图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《俄瑞斯忒亚》中有很多血，但那是另一种血：尼采作品中的血，就像卡斯特卢奇作品中被剥皮的野兽的血一样。大声思考的话，也许我的参考对象是女性的，因为那是生命的血，而我在意的是它不被隐藏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我不支持为了展示而展示的裸露，甚至不是纯粹美学意义上的。我不支持压抑所有属于生命的东西。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在与被视为泰斗的导演合作时，你是否曾提出过与他们不同的解读，并看到它留在了演出中？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“和龙贡在一起时我还很年轻。我基本上信任导演，我真的需要这种信任。一开始是他们选择了我；最近我也送了自己一份由我来选择的礼物。我和一些导演有一种对话，有时我会说：这件事情我们解不开，你觉得我可以这样试试吗？很多时候我的提议会被接受，但它始终是一个实用的、解决问题的提议。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在获得Hystrio奖和Ubu奖之后，你收到的邀约改变了吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«我把它们当作一次轻抚：它们到一个大为成熟的阶段才到来，这也是因为发生在我身上的种种事情，那些在每个人生活中都会发生的事。对我而言，意义重大的是，在经历多年感受到观众的认可之后，业内人士和记者的认可也到来了。它们意味着一个更全面的拥抱。并且，非常不错的邀约正在到来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我将与莱昂纳多·利迪（Leonardo Lidi）合作出演《欲望号街车》。在《猫》之后，我并未把他的再次邀请视作理所当然。我还将与托尔卡希尔（Tolcachir）合作一部新戏。此外，一个项目正在酝酿中：《你未曾带我去的方向》，改编自玛丽亚·格拉齐亚·卡兰德罗内（Maria Grazia Calandrone）的小说。这个创意是我想出来的，弗兰科·帕伦蒂剧院（Teatro Franco Parenti）进行制作，埃伊瑙迪（Einaudi）授予了我版权。它将于春季在帕伦蒂剧院首演。我甚至还在参加试镜，这可是我以前从未做过的事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "总有一天，我也许会——不是说去当导演……但我心里一直有个关于雷蒙德·卡佛（Raymond Carver）的项目。而且我会做一些工作坊：我很想有一次站在台下，最好能指导一下年轻人。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有没有哪个项目是你希望从某种迫切感出发来展开的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text":
